**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects: two fallback tests make their GPU unavailable.** `strand-render/tests/effects.rs::aurora_is_still_and_cpu_fallbacks_are_noticed_once` and `strand/src/demo/host.rs::tests::effect_fallbacks_are_said_once_as_notices` test the notices of a user with no GPU; in a `gpu` build a renderer that has heard nothing yet may still get one, so each now delivers a `GpuReply::Unavailable` first. **2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects (review): a failed bundled pass draws its CPU version.** A pass that fails on a working device (`GpuReply::Failed` with its key: over the device's texture size, a driver's compile error, a readback error) was recorded as one transparent pixel, which every bundled effect then took as its pixels: a filter layer drew a one-pixel group, glass and a large blur a one-pixel backdrop, aurora and particles nothing, with no notice and until the want's key changed. A failure is now recorded as such (`ShaderResults::failed`): it still keeps the want from being asked again while its inputs stay, and a `shader` node still draws nothing (it has no CPU version), but `ShaderResults::usable` never offers it, so a bundled effect draws the CPU version design.md gives it (bloom a glow, glass blur and tint, the others unfiltered, aurora still, particles capped). A tilt turns in 3-D only after a filter pass of its node gave pixels (`ShaderResults::answered`) and while its last one did not fail; once one failed it turns in 2-D and asks for no warm-up pass until the node goes. `tests/gpu_effects.rs::a_failed_bundled_pass_draws_its_cpu_version` (each of bloom, CRT, chromatic, wobble, glass, a large blur, aurora and particles: the frame after the failure is the CPU's, and nothing is asked again), `::a_tilt_whose_pass_fails_stays_2d`. Both run without a device: the test answers the passes.

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects (review): a pass's pixels are held only while a frame wants them.** Results were pruned only when their node left the tree, and not at all for a surface whose frame wanted nothing, so a hidden glass, a large blur (at least 800 KB, several MB at 1440p), a filter layer or a tilt at rest kept its full-resolution read-back pixels as long as the node existed. Each result now records the surface that asked for it, and every frame of a surface drops that surface's results its wants no longer name (before the early return when it wants nothing); a surface that goes away drops its results at the next tick. A failure's record (a shared one-pixel pixmap) stays while its node does, so it is not asked again. These pixels are not counted in the offscreen groups' 4 MB: design.md's 4 MB is the CPU's cache of groups it rasterised, while these are a pass's output held only while the effect shows, like a `shader` node's pixels, and they belong to the GPU path's own cost (design.md's +20–40 MB while promoted). A pixmap per showing effect is the floor for drawing it at all; what was wrong was keeping it after. `Renderer::gpu_pass_bytes` (tests) and `::bundled_effects_start_the_gpu_only_while_visible` check it is non-zero while each effect shows and zero once hidden. `strand/tests/gpu_idle.rs`'s promoted panel now carries a `filter: bloom(8)` box while `on`, so its PSS-across-cycles check (3 MiB) runs the layer readback path too.

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects (review): a tilt's warm-up pass waits until the node shows.** The one-pixel pass that starts the device for a 3-D tilt was asked whenever the lean turned, before the visibility check, and the lean turns with the pointer anywhere on the surface: a tilt clipped out (a row scrolled out of a clipping list) started the device, and retried every 30 s without one. It is now asked only while the node shows, the same test every other effect uses. `::bundled_effects_start_the_gpu_only_while_visible` now covers all eight (the tilt, with the pointer on the bar, and the large backdrop blur added) plus a `.wgsl` noise field, each hidden both off the bar and clipped out by an ancestor's `clip` while on it. Two harness changes keep it independent of wall-clock pacing: render's `set_promotion(false)` (tests) keeps the 1300 px surface the large blur needs on the CPU however long its frames take, and the idle window is shortened only after the visible phase, so a slow frame cannot drop the device mid-test. Both were latent in the earlier version (the large blur test promoted once in a loaded run).

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects (review): "aurora and noise fields" is one item, aurora bundled and a noise field a `.wgsl` shader.** design.md:524 lists "aurora and noise fields" as one of the eight but gives a noise field no spelling: the built-in effects are `lightning | sparks | shimmer | ripple | aurora` (design.md:510), the filters and backdrops without a node of their own are named (bloom, crt, chromatic, wobble, glass), and `noise(x)` is a time signal for props, not a node. Inventing `effect noise` or `filter: noise()` would add a concept the design does not have. So the item is read as aurora, which is the bundled shader (`effect aurora`, a field of curtains moving with `t`), plus noise fields written as `.wgsl` shaders, which "use the same path" (design.md:524): drawn by the GPU, started only while visible, released 30 s after. The visibility test runs a time-reading noise-field shader beside the eight. If the owner wants a bundled noise field with its own spelling, that is a design.md change first.

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects (review): files outside S-gpu's ownership.** m4-plan gives S-gpu `promote.rs`, `canvas.rs` and `renderer/backend.rs` in strand-render, yet wave 3 has it land "the 8 bundled effects with S-effects' CPU fallbacks", and the effects meet the CPU where the flattener and the fallbacks are. An earlier report on this branch said only two files outside its crates changed; that was wrong. This branch changes, in S-runtime's files: `flatten/{mod,node,hash}.rs` (pass wants made while a node shows, the tilt's 3-D switch), the new `flatten/gpu.rs` (the bundled wants and drawing their pixels), `layers.rs` (`Layer::gpu`), `offscreen.rs` (a GPU layer's pixels used as its group; `render_group`'s bundled flag and `rasterise` split out), `renderer/{frame,wake}.rs` (one argument), `renderer/{mod,layout_pass}.rs` (`gpu_ok`, the GPU hooks), `anim/{mod,motion}.rs` (uniforms spring, the lean's four channels); in S-effects' files: `effects/{mod,lean,particles}.rs` (the knobs, the tilt pass, the lean's channels, particles' GPU uniforms), one-line changes in `effects/{builtin,light,transition}.rs`, `anim/keyframes.rs` and `backdrop.rs`, and the new `effects/gpu.rs`; in the compiler, `builtin.schema`'s bundled knobs and their tests; and `strand/src/demo/host.rs` (recorded above). Each change is the smallest seam the effect needed, and none changes the behaviour of the owner's code without a GPU (the CPU-only build's tests are unchanged apart from the two fallback tests above). S-effects is also active in wave 3, so these files may conflict at merge: the integrator should merge S-effects first and have this branch rebased, with S-runtime and S-effects reviewing the hunks in their files.

Rerun after the review fixes as `STRAND_STRICT_GPU=1 scripts/container/gpu.sh cargo test --release -p strand --test gpu_idle` on the laptop's Intel GPU (ANV, `Readback` mode as before), with the panel's new `filter: bloom(8)` box: it passed. PSS 24,560 kB before the GPU and 29,196 kB after the first drop, 4,636 kB over the baseline, inside the leg's 6,144 kB (m4-gpu-w2 measured 4,455 kB); of that, 1,864 kB is strand's own code paged in, 822 kB libstdc++, 1,284 kB anonymous and mimalloc memory. The second cycle ended at 31,068 kB, 1,872 kB over the first, inside the 3 MiB no-growth bound. Strips matched the CPU's in both cycles (0 pixels past 6, worst channel difference 3). **2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects (review 2): a failed pass is keyed without its time.** A failed bundled pass was "not asked again until its inputs change", but a clocked pass (wobble, aurora, particles) has `strand.time` in its want's key, and particles' uniforms carry their positions, so it was asked again every frame, each failure logging a warning and aurora keeping its refresh clock over a still CPU frame. A want now carries a `base` as well as its key: the key without the time and the pointer, and for a clocked bundled pass without its uniforms. A failed pass is asked again only when its `base` changes (its code, size, scale or input; for an unclocked one also its uniforms). For a clocked pass that means a changed colour or rate does not retry it either, until its size or input changes or the node goes; that is preferred over retrying a failing driver at refresh rate. While its pass's last answer is a failure, a node takes its CPU form whole: wobble has no clock, aurora no refresh clock, and the still-aurora and capped-particle notices are said (`Flattener::gpu_draws`).

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects (review 2): a tilt warms up again after the device goes.** `ShaderResults::answered`, which turns a tilt in 3-D, outlived the device, so a tilt hovered after the 30 s idle drop drew its card flat until a new device answered (hundreds of ms on lavapipe). When the device goes (dropped on idle, lost, unavailable), a node keeps `answered` only if it still holds its 3-D pixels (a tilt shown at rest, which keeps drawing them); any other warms up in 2-D again, as on its first hover. Clearing it while the device stays up was rejected: the frame then holds for the up device's answer, which takes one round trip, so the first hover's 2-D warm-up is not needed there.

No syntax was added.

**2026-10-10 · m4-gpu-effects (review 2): the idle test proves its bloom.** `gpu_idle`'s `filter: bloom(8)` box was not checked, so the test would pass if its pass never ran or fell back. Its box is now #f5c2e7 beside a plain box of the same colour, and each cycle waits for the bloomed box to be brighter inside than the plain one by at least 24 (summed channels): the GPU's bloom screens the glow over the box (+78 measured on lavapipe), while the CPU's fallback glow is drawn under it and leaves the inside as plain.
## m4-interaction-finish

**2026-10-10 · m4-interaction-finish: a layer surface's origin is arranged past our own exclusive zones, in global layout coordinates.** The wave-2 origin placed every layer surface over its whole output, so a tray panel anchored under a 36 px bar reported y = 0 and the app's menu opened over the bar; and origins were output-local, so a press on a second output sent a point on the first. `placement::arranged_area` now follows wlroots' `arrange_layers` (the order sway, labwc and river share; niri and Hyprland reserve the same way for the anchors a shell uses): exclusive surfaces first, layer by layer from `overlay` down, each reserving its zone plus its margin on its edge, a zone of -1 taking the whole output. Only our own surfaces are known; another program's bar is not (the protocol never says where a surface ended up), which the module doc records. Origins add the output's logical position, the space `SNI Activate(x, y)` and xdg positioners outside a popup use. Proved by `sway.rs::layer_surfaces_are_placed_past_our_zones_in_layout_coordinates` (grim reads the panel where its origin says, on two outputs, and back at y = 0 when the bar goes).

**2026-10-10 · m4-interaction-finish: a tray action called by no input sends (0, 0).** The click point was a process-wide "last press" that every `tray.activate` read, so a timer or an `strand ipc` write activating an item sent the point of whatever was pressed minutes before. The point is now read when the action is built (`TrayCall`, the service's action type) and only when the calling thread runs a handler of an input event: the VM counts the handlers of `click`, `secondary`, `middle`, `scroll`, `activate`, `key`, `dismiss` and `drop` it runs (`vm::in_input_handler`), and the binary hands that probe to the tray at startup, so strand-services keeps no dependency on the compiler. (0, 0) is what the SNI spec's hosts send when they have no point; KDE's and waybar's items treat it as "place it yourself". A handler that awaits keeps its flag only for the synchronous part it runs before its first await, which is where a click's action is called. Proved by `tray.rs::the_tray_is_the_watcher_when_there_is_none` (an action outside an input scope sends `Activate at 0,0`) and `instantiate.rs::actions_know_whether_input_called_them`.

**2026-10-10 · m4-interaction-finish: Hyprland is known by its globals, not by `HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE`.** Two behaviours hang on Hyprland: it draws a layer surface stretched to its arranged box whatever its viewport (so a root's `scale` pose is painted there, decisions.md m4-surface-w2) and it blurs layer surfaces by its own rules (so the blur fallback's reason names `strand compositor-rules`). Neither is a protocol capability a client can query: no global says "honours `wp_viewport` on layer surfaces", and testing it would mean reading the screen back through screencopy at startup, a round trip and a permission for one bit. What can be fixed is where the answer comes from: the environment variable is inherited by anything started from a Hyprland session, so a nested sway or a `strand run` against another compositor's socket was treated as Hyprland and painted its scale. The registry is the connection's own: `caps::Offered::from_registry` marks `CompositorCaps::hyprland` when any `hyprland_*` global (Hyprland's own protocols, which every release since 0.3x offers: `hyprland_focus_grab_manager_v1`, `hyprland_surface_manager_v1`, ...) is listed. The matrix asserts it is set on Hyprland only (`surfaces_meet_the_live_compositor`), and the pose branches there read it. niri's lack of the alpha modifier is proven by `compositor_matrix.rs::a_posed_panel_looks_the_same_on_every_compositor`: `strand run` with a half-opacity, half-scale panel blends the desktop halfway to white in the half-size box and leaves the rest of the box alone on sway and labwc (delegated), niri (painted; the test fails if niri starts offering the modifier, so it keeps proving the repaint path) and Hyprland (opacity delegated, scale painted; CI).

**2026-10-10 · m4-interaction-finish: password redaction remembers replaced values and redacts on fragments.** `Secrets` redacted only the inputs' current values once no password input was mounted, and forgot a value the moment its field emptied or its input went away, so a state that copied the password (`last = secret` before `secret = ""`) faulting after the unlock printed it, and a slice of it (`secret.slice(2, 6)`) or an upper-cased copy printed whenever no input was mounted. Now a value replaced by one it does not start is remembered (typing on adds nothing; a value inside a kept one is not kept twice), the newest four of them, as zeroized `Password`s; and a message still holding any 4-byte run of a known value, ASCII case ignored (a shorter password: the whole of it), is redacted whole. Four bytes is the trade: shorter runs would redact ordinary messages for any common pair of letters, longer would let a four-letter slice through; a false positive costs one log line's text, never behaviour. Keeping old values in memory outlives the lock (see the review paragraph below for the residual risk this records). Proved by `run/lock.rs::tests::a_password_fragment_is_never_logged` and the updated `password_values_are_redacted`, `a_fault_that_can_carry_values_is_redacted_whole_while_a_password_is_mounted`.

**2026-10-10 · m4-interaction-finish: the supervisor requirement is documented with a unit and proven in the lock VM.** A process death while locked (main-thread panic, abort, SIGKILL) cannot be survived from inside the process, so architecture.md's residual risk stands: strand needs a supervisor. What was missing was proof that a supervisor is enough. `tests/lock.rs::a_supervised_strand_dying_while_locked_keeps_the_session_locked` runs strand under a restart loop that behaves as systemd's `Restart=on-failure` (restart on a non-zero exit or a signal, stop on a clean exit), kills it with SIGKILL while locked and with SIGABRT once it is back, and asserts from grim that the desktop never shows between each kill and the restarted strand's password field, that the test itself never starts strand, and that the right password unlocks and removes the marker. architecture.md now carries the user unit to use (`Restart=on-failure`, `RestartSec=0`). strand still ships no supervisor of its own: a second process watching the first adds a concept and a failure mode the session manager already covers.

**2026-10-10 · m4-interaction-finish: the blur ladder's inspector half is a `strand watch` notice per `blur` box.** The inspector proper (pick, identity, provenance) is M5's; what the blur ladder owes it is "the inspector says why" a `blur` fell back. The surface that exists today for per-node answers is `strand watch`, where runtime faults already carry `file:line:col`. So when the compositor is known not to blur, the host walks a surface's tree (nested popups left to their own surfaces) the first time its frame has blur regions, and again whenever their count changes, and sends logic each `blur` node with its kind and whether it draws the tint (`ToLogic::BlurFallback`); logic resolves each node through `Instance::origin` and makes one notice per box: `<file>:<line>:<col>: `box` in strand-Top asks for blur and draws its tint fallback (alpha + 0.15; `blur_fallback: none` turns it off): <why>` (or "draws no blur and no tint (`blur_fallback: none`)"), deduplicated and kept for watchers that subscribe later like every main-thread notice. `why` is `caps::blur_missing`, the reason without what the box draws, so a `blur_fallback: none` box is not told it draws a tint. The once-per-run warning stays as it was. The walk costs one tree pass per surface per change of its region count, only while the compositor does not blur; the region count itself is read each frame only then. M5's inspector reads the same notices.

**2026-10-10 · m4-interaction-finish: how Hyprland's blur mixes with Strand's.** CI's Hyprland 0.56.2 offers `ext-background-effect-v1` with blur (the matrix reports `background_effect: true` and 21 blur rectangles), so on current Hyprland the ladder's first rung applies: Strand sends each `blur` box's rounded region and draws no tint, exactly as on niri. The layer rules `strand compositor-rules` prints (`blur`, `blur_popups`, `ignore_alpha 0.5` per namespace) are a second, independent mechanism: Hyprland blurs behind every pixel of the matched surface whose alpha is above 0.5, whatever the region says. With both in place the blur is no longer limited to the `blur` boxes: an opaque-enough box without `blur` on the same surface gets blurred too, and the rounded shape no longer bounds it. Without the protocol (older Hyprland) the rules are the only blur, and Strand cannot tell whether they were pasted, so it keeps its tint (alpha + 0.15) on top: a box whose background is under 0.5 alpha can cross the rule's threshold only because of the tint, and a box above it ends 0.15 more opaque than on a protocol compositor (`blur_fallback: none` restores parity for such boxes). Decided: nothing is detected or switched automatically (no protocol says a layer rule applies); the printed rules now open with a comment saying they are only for a Hyprland without `ext-background-effect-v1` and what they do besides where it is offered, and the fallback reason names the rules only when the protocol is missing (it already did). Hyprland is known by its `hyprland_*` globals (see above), never by the environment.

**2026-10-10 · m4-interaction-finish: a carried drag shows the source as its icon, which supersedes m4-lists-w2's "no icon".** m4-lists-w2 left the icon out as a second render target for a cosmetic gain. It costs less than that: `Renderer::drag_image` flattens only the dragged node as a root with its lift and glide held and no animation stepped, rasterises its box into a CPU buffer of the box's size, once per drag, so there is no second live target and nothing redraws while the pointer moves (the compositor moves the icon). The icon is committed after `start_drag` on the icon surface with the grab point as its offset, because sway places an icon committed before the drag at the pointer with no offset. A fractional scale is drawn through the viewporter like other surfaces. Headless sway 1.9 leaves the last icon frame on screen after a drop until the pointer moves; the tests move it before checking the icon is gone instead of making up a commit for the compositor.

**2026-10-10 · m4-interaction-finish: what a drag gives other programs travels in `Prop::Drag`.** The surface manager needs the source's data when another program asks, and the value lives on the logic thread. Rather than a new cross-thread request, the compiler puts the exportable form beside the type name (`List [type, kind, text…]`) for the three things design.md says cross program boundaries (text, files, apps: a `text` value, a `Drop` record and an `App`); every other value keeps the bare `Keyword` and exports nothing. Readers go through `strand_scene::drag_type`/`drag_export`, so the encoding stays in one place. Files go out as `text/uri-list` (percent-encoded `file://` URIs) and also as their paths as text; an app as its `.desktop` file's URI when one is found under `XDG_DATA_HOME`/`XDG_DATA_DIRS`, and its id as text.

**2026-10-10 · m4-interaction-finish: another Strand process's drag arrives as a `Drop`.** A node id means nothing in another process, and design.md types drops from other programs as `Drop`. So a drag whose private type starts with `application/x-strand-node;` but names another process is read through what it exports, like any program's drag, and logged at debug as another Strand; with nothing exportable (a `Pin`) it carries nothing readable and is refused like any such offer. Sending typed Strand values across processes would add a serialisation format design.md does not have.

**2026-10-10 · m4-interaction-finish: `Prop::DropRows` replaces "make it a `list`".** m4-lists-w2 placed a plain container of non-draggable `for` items in its parent, because render could not tell `for` children from content. The compiler can: it sets `Prop::DropRows` on an `on drop` target with a direct `for` child, and render counts drops among a target's children when it is a `list`, holds `drag:` children, or has `DropRows`. This removes the need to tell users to wrap such a target in a `list`; a per-item target with its own content still has no `DropRows` and is placed among its parent's rows.

**2026-10-10 · m4-interaction-finish: review of the redaction: a floor, escapes and a recorded core-dump risk.** Three findings held. (1) Values under four bytes were remembered and matched whole, so one letter typed and cleared ("a", then "") blanked every later fault message holding an "a". Now a value under `FRAGMENT` (4) bytes is neither remembered nor matched: below four bytes a match cannot tell a password from ordinary text, and while its input is mounted a password of any length is still covered by the blanket rule (every value-carrying error replaced whole). (2) The fragment match was on raw bytes with ASCII case folding, so a password with a quote or backslash every three bytes, or a non-ASCII one upper-cased, printed through Debug or JSON escaping. The message is now compared in two forms, lower-cased with Unicode `to_lowercase`, as written and with `\\ \" \' \n \r \t \0 \u{..} \uXXXX` undone; letters whose upper case is longer (`ß`/`SS`) still escape it, which architecture.md's wording now allows. (3) The paragraph above said keeping old values widened nothing; after a submit the field is empty, so the remembered values are the one sure copy of up to four recent passwords for the rest of the process. Dropping them when the last password input unmounts would undo the change: while an input is mounted every value-carrying error is redacted whole anyway, so remembered values only ever act after the unmount. Decided: keep them, and record the residual risk in architecture.md ("The lock"): a core dump after an unlock can hold them; a session that cares sets `LimitCORE=0` on the unit. Making strand non-dumpable while it holds them (as `strand-auth` is) was rejected: it also takes away `/proc/<pid>` and ptrace from the user for the whole session, and the cores it prevents are the ones that diagnose the crash. Proved by `run/lock.rs::tests::a_password_fragment_is_never_logged` (a typo cleared redacts nothing; escaped, JSON-escaped and non-ASCII upper-cased copies are redacted).

**2026-10-10 · m4-interaction-finish: review of the input flag, blur notices and the drag icon.** (1) The input-handler flag was entered again on every resume of a handler's coroutine, so `on click { await sleep(10s); tray.activate(item) }` read whatever point was current ten seconds later; the flag is now entered for the first stretch only, as the tray paragraph above already said (`instantiate.rs::actions_know_whether_input_called_them` clicks a handler that calls after an `await` and finds that call outside the input). (2) Blur notices were logged before their dedupe, once per box on every report, and a scrolling windowed `list` of `blur` items changes the region count and so reports often; and they were never retired. They now live apart from the other main-thread notices: logic keeps the last report per surface, logs and sends only notices not said before, and after a committed reload says them again from the kept reports for the nodes still mounted, at their new places, dropping a removed or moved box's old line (`run/tests.rs::each_blur_box_says_where_it_is_and_why_it_fell_back` reloads a moved and a removed box). The host still walks the surface's tree when the count changes: the walk is one pass over one surface, the same order of work as the flatten that just ran, and only while the compositor does not blur; tracking which boxes changed would need the walk anyway. A soft reload that swaps a `blur` box for a new node at an unchanged count is told at the next change of the count (a hard reload recreates the surfaces, which reports afresh). (3) The drag icon was rasterised into a surface-sized buffer (about 33 MB for a 4K panel) and cropped; `Raster::paint_window` now paints straight into a buffer of the box's size, rasterising each pixel by the same fixed-grid cell as a full paint (offscreen groups still drawn over the whole surface), so the icon stays bit-identical to the frame (`tests/drag.rs::the_drag_icon_is_the_source_drawn_alone_at_rest` compares it with the crop of the full frame, at an offset off the cell grid, and with its PNG).

**2026-10-10 · m4-interaction-finish: the documented unit lifts systemd's start limit and backs off instead; the test's supervisor is that unit.** Review found that the unit architecture.md recommended (`Restart=on-failure`, `RestartSec=0`) kept systemd's default start limit, 5 starts in 10 s. A strand that died again soon after each restart while locked would get the unit marked failed after a few milliseconds, leaving the compositor's abandoned lock with no password field: the state the supervisor exists to end. The test's restart loop restarted forever, so it never showed this. The unit now sets `StartLimitIntervalSec=0` in `[Unit]`, and the brake moves to the restart delay: `RestartSec=100ms` growing over `RestartSteps=5` to `RestartMaxDelaySec=2s` (systemd 254; older systemd ignores those two keys and waits 100 ms each time). A strand that cannot start then costs one start every 2 s, not a busy loop, and the field is back at most 2 s after any death plus strand's start. The earlier reason for `RestartSec=0`, that 100 ms only delays the field, holds; but with no start limit a zero delay would spin forever. The test's supervisor is no longer a hand-written loop. `tests/lock.rs` reads the ini block from architecture.md itself (`Supervisor::documented`) and runs a shell loop with systemd's semantics: restart on failure, delays as `RestartSteps` interpolates them, and systemd's default start limit for what the unit leaves out. `the_supervisor_gives_up_as_systemd_does_unless_the_unit_lifts_the_limit` shows the loop giving up after five quick deaths under a unit with no limit, and checks that the documented unit has none. The lock-VM test now adds a crash loop of six deaths after its two rounds, each death as soon as the new strand runs. With `StartLimitIntervalSec=0` removed from the doc, that test fails with "start limit hit (5 starts in 10000 ms)" (run once by hand); with it, the session stays locked and the field returns.

**2026-10-10 · m4-interaction-finish: only press-caused handlers take the tray's click point.** Review said `key`, `activate` and `dismiss` handlers took the last mouse press's point. For `key` and `activate` that was already false: the host sets the point to (0, 0) on every key press (m4-surface-w2, `demo/host.rs::a_press_sets_the_tray_click_point`), so Return on a row or a key handler sends (0, 0), and a clicked row's `activate` should send the click's point, which it does. The real stale cases were the events no press of ours precedes: `dismiss` (a click away the compositor saw elsewhere, or focus loss), `scroll` (a wheel sets no point) and `drop` (the press started the drag on another node, or in another program). `vm::INPUT_EVENTS` is now `click`, `secondary`, `middle`, `activate` and `key`, so a tray action from the other three sends (0, 0). `instantiate.rs::only_press_caused_handlers_run_as_input` drives each event's handler.

**2026-10-10 · m4-interaction-finish: an exclusive zone that goes to none or moves places the others where it was.** `place_layer` placed the other surfaces on the output again only while the surface's zone was positive, and only on its current output. A live bar whose zone dropped to none (`height: 0`), or a surface that moved to another output, left the panels it had pushed down at origins that still took the old zone out. Their tray click points were then off by the bar's height. Each surface now remembers the monitor its zone was last counted on (`Surface::zone_on`). Placing it places the others on both the old and the new monitor when they differ, and a removal uses it too. A spec change places the configured surface at once instead of waiting for a configure. On sway the others got a configure anyway (sway configures every layer surface when it arranges), so the proof is on the fake, which configures a surface only when its own request changes, as a compositor may. The fake gained an opt-in `zxdg_output_manager_v1` (`SurfaceGlobals::xdg_output`) for the logical sizes the placing needs. `fake.rs::a_zone_that_drops_to_none_places_the_others_again` fails without the change. `sway.rs::layer_surfaces_are_placed_past_our_zones_in_layout_coordinates` gained the same steps on sway.

## m4-integration-w3

**2026-10-10 · m4-integration-w3: merge order and the offscreen pass that both effects branches rewrote.** The wave-3 integration merged laptop/m4-effects-finish first, then laptop/m4-gpu-effects, then laptop/m4-interaction-finish, as m4-gpu-effects asked (it edits S-effects' and S-runtime's files, recorded under its own section). A merge with `--no-ff` instead of a rebase keeps every stream's commits as they were reviewed. Both effects branches rewrote `Offscreen::prepare`'s group loop. effects-finish replaced the two passes (groups, then backdrops) with one pass ordered by where each group ends, so a backdrop inside an offscreen ancestor shows what is behind it. gpu-effects added a GPU group's read-back pixels and skipped GPU backdrops in the second pass. The merge keeps effects-finish's single ordered pass and puts gpu-effects' check at its top: a layer with `gpu` pixels takes them and is not drawn by the CPU, whether it is a filter group or a backdrop. Its pixels are then in `current` for the groups still open around it, as a CPU backdrop's are. `render_group` keeps gpu-effects' split (`rasterise` plus the filters, with the `bundled` flag) and applies effects-finish's `pixelate` mosaic before the CPU filters in both cases, so a GPU pass's input is mosaicked like the CPU blur and colour filters that already run before the bundled passes. `Layer::cell_local` needs both `mosaic` and `gpu` to be empty. The other conflicts were both sides added side by side (Layer fields, module lists, `Animator::jelly` next to `hold_still`/`release`, the host's per-surface maps, the features.md boxes, the decisions.md sections).

## m4-audit

**2026-10-10 · m4-audit: the lock exit is ticked on a lock VM run of the integration tree, with the helper killed and deleted for real.** The exit stayed unticked with no reason after the merges, and its newest VM evidence (23 tests) predated the supervisor tests. m4-plan's tier C asks for "the helper OOM-killed or deleted"; `auth_crash` is an `abort()` inside the helper, which the client sees exactly as it sees a SIGKILL (end of file on the socket), so it stands in for the OOM kill as far as the client can tell, but two tests now do it for real: `pam_helper_killed_mid_check_shows_the_fallback` SIGKILLs the helper from outside once it has read the right password and hung (the new strand fault `auth_hold` keeps the default 30 s timeout under `auth_hang`, so the kill, not the timeout, ends the check; the test asserts the log says "the PAM helper stopped"), and `pam_helper_deleted_and_killed_keeps_the_session_locked_until_it_is_back` moves the helper binary away (renamed beside itself and put back by a guard, since the build directory is the host's) and kills the running one (from a copy of `strand` and its helper in the test's own directory, `Vm::installed`: CI's checkout belongs to the runner's user, so the guest's test user cannot rename anything in cargo's directory, which failed the first CI run of the test). The second found a real gap: the fallback's `strand-lock-auth` thread looked for the helper once, at its first check, so a helper deleted at that moment (a package upgrade mid-session) left the fallback unable to check any password for the rest of the lock session. It now looks again at each check until one is found; while none exists every password is refused (the session stays locked, which is the fail-closed reading). `scripts/lockvm/scenarios/all.sh` passed on 2026-10-10 at 70af44f: session_lock 7, strand_lock 27 of 27, faillock and pam.

**2026-10-10 · m4-audit: "no grim pixel shows the desktop" now means every pixel.** `Shot::desktop()` sampled one pixel of the test desktop's bar. The locked assertions (`until_locked`, `Vm::lock`, the no-locker and supervisor checks) now scan the whole shot for the bar's colour (`Shot::desktop_anywhere`, tolerance 3), so a lock covering part of an output fails. `Shot::desktop()` stays for "the desktop is back", where one pixel is enough.

**2026-10-10 · m4-audit: a GPU submission that never ends loses the device; a hung presented surface and a GPU stall while locked stay open for the owner.** naga bounds neither loops nor run time, and lavapipe has no driver reset, so a validated shader with an endless loop blocked the GPU thread forever in a readback's `poll(wait_indefinitely)`. Readbacks (passes and readback frames) now wait at most `HUNG_AFTER` (10 s, far past any real frame or pass, even lavapipe's on a loaded machine; a false alarm costs a CPU fallback): the pass answers `Failed` with its key (so render records it as failed and does not ask for it again), then `Lost` ("stopped answering") and `Exited`, and the thread leaks the device, renderer and swapchains rather than dropping them (a drop waits for the queue). `strand-gpu/tests/hang.rs` proves it on lavapipe. Not done, and recorded for the owner because each needs a design call: (1) a promoted `GpuPresent` surface does not read back, so a frame that hangs there is not caught by this deadline (the WSI's own acquire timeout is the only bound), and nothing exempts a lock's surfaces from promotion; (2) the lock's fault list (`run/lock.rs`, `reason()`) does not count a GPU stall as a fault, so a fullscreen clocked shader in a `lock` that hangs after its first frame on a promoted surface can freeze the lock's content without showing the fallback. The options are to never promote lock surfaces (their passes would read back, which this deadline covers) or to watch for a `Presented` that never comes while locked; either changes design.md's promotion rule or the lock's fault list.

**2026-10-10 · m4-audit: the GPU thread's caches are bounded.** `pass_reads` gained an entry per pass key (which includes the node's generation) and `Passes::pipelines` one per shader text, and neither was ever evicted while the device lived; a shown shader keeps the device alive, so remounted shader nodes and every hot-reload save grew them for the session. Both are now a small least-recently-used map (`strand-gpu/src/lru.rs`): 64 pipelines, far more than one screen draws, and 16 readback buffers keyed by size instead of pass key, since a pass's read finishes before the next pass is drawn and passes of one size can share a buffer. No interface change: render does not have to tell the thread which passes are gone.

**2026-10-10 · m4-audit: the 2,000-row e2e test keeps reporting stalls, not asserting them.** Render never shows past the mounted rows (m4-lists-w1), so logic lag shows as `stalls=`, never `gaps=`, and the e2e test's per-frame `gaps=0` catches only holes among mounted rows. Asserting `stalls == 0` on the real binary would make a functional assertion of how fast a debug logic thread answers on a shared runner, which CLAUDE.md forbids; the bench (`list_scroll_bench.rs`, a logic answering 50 ms late, `stalls == 0`) stays the assertion, and features.md's exit text now says which check covers what. The e2e test's bursts were flaky for another reason (run 38028157777: 3,800 of 96,976 pixels late): `still()` now also waits for the burst's own frame (`top` five rows on) and for nothing left on render's workers (the damage line's new `pending=` field, `Renderer::work_pending`: text layouts or image decodes in flight), before its quiet window.

**2026-10-10 · m4-audit: flakes fixed without wall-clock bounds.** `compositor_matrix.rs`'s `agree()` takes the state each step expects (an action is fire-and-forget, so both sides could still agree on the old focus: sway 1.12 in CI run 38040362877). `animated.rs` writes its three shared animations once per process (parallel tests truncated and rewrote them under each other's decoders: run 38034659682), and its clock-wake test measures each wake from before the paint that set it. `image.rs`'s file-job test holds its job on a channel until the in-flight case is checked (run 38037844854). strand-introspect's non-blocking ask is proved by a gate the caller must not wait on, not by `elapsed() < 40 ms`. `image_idle_hook.rs` judges the owed hook by when the hook itself ran, measured from before the request, so load can only make it pass. Left as they are: `strand-scene/src/tokens.rs::huge_fan_out_fails_fast` (< 500 ms for a work-budgeted lookup) and `strand-dev/tests/lsp.rs` (< 1,500 ms before diagnostics against a bus that never answers) keep a wall-clock assertion with a wide margin; neither has flaked, and replacing them (an evaluation counter, a fake bus that answers on command) belongs to their crates' owners.

**2026-10-10 · m4-audit: smaller fixes.** `strand-gpu/tests/lifecycle.rs`'s test is renamed `the_thread_and_driver_start_at_spawn_and_end_at_shutdown`: it calls `start()` and ends with `Shutdown`, so it never proved the first-visible-effect start or the idle drop (strand-render's tests do, and features.md now cites them for that); older entries above keep the old name. The helper no longer prints its own `login`-fallback warning on every start (its stderr is strand's and it starts on every lock and fault); the client's once-per-process warning from the hello is design.md's "one-time warning". A thumbnail frame is read from a read-only mapping of its memfd, sealed against shrinking so no holder of the fd can fault the read, and scaled in the buffer's orientation before only the small result is turned upright: no full-size copy per frame (33 MB for a 4K window at up to 15 frames a second, twice when rotated). architecture.md's render module map, its threads table (`strand-lock-auth`) and its `strand-gpu` reply text, README's status and crate table, m4-plan's lock and GPU exit sections and handoff.md are brought up to the built tree.

**2026-10-10 · m4-audit: a lock with no way out is a check error.** A `lock` that draws, keeps its logic alive and never faults never shows the built-in field, so `lock { text clock.now }`, or a lock whose field submits through a handler that never calls `auth`, locked the session with only a TTY for a way out (and the restart marker locked again on the next start). design.md's "fails closed" promises a way out whenever something goes wrong; a config with no path to `auth.submit` is wrong before it runs, so the check refuses it: `check::lock_no_auth` is an error when nothing in the lock calls `auth.submit`, searched through its handlers and timers (every `if`/`match`/`for` branch, so a field revealed on a key press counts) and the components it shows. A `fn` cannot call an action (`check::impure`), so fns are not searched; a call outside the lock (a bar's handler) does not count, since only the lock has the keyboard while locked. It is judged only on a program with no other error, so a misspelt `auth.sumbit` gives its own error, not two. A runtime rule ("no password `input` mounted, show the fallback") was rejected: a lock that shows a clock and reveals its field on a key press is the common shape and would show the fallback over itself. The check does not prove the call is reached at run time (a handler on an element never shown, a branch never taken); it removes the config that has no call at all, which is the one design.md's wording cannot excuse. Tests: `checker.rs::a_lock_needs_a_reachable_auth_submit`, `negative/lock_no_auth.strand`; the unit tests' locks gained an `on key` submit.
